title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Overview: industry outlook and exogenous vulnerability
key_points: Boeing states the industry remains vulnerable to exogenous developments, listing fuel price spikes, credit market shocks, acts of terrorism, natural disasters, conflicts, epidemics, pandemics and increased global environmental regulations.
Boeing's Commercial Market Outlook projects a 3.8% growth rate for passenger and cargo traffic over a 20-year period, based on long-term global GDP growth projections of 2.6% average annual.
Boeing projects demand for approximately 41,170 new airplanes over the next 20 years.
BGS commercial services volume recovered to pre-pandemic levels during 2022.
raw_excerpt: The industry remains vulnerable to exogenous developments including fuel price spikes, credit market shocks, acts of terrorism, natural disasters, conflicts, epidemics, pandemics and increased global environmental regulations.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Overview: airline financial performance drives new-capacity demand
key_points: Boeing states that airline financial performance influences demand for new capacity.
Per IATA cited by Boeing: airline industry net losses were $138 billion in 2020 and $42 billion in 2021.
IATA forecast $6.9 billion of global industry losses for 2022, with about $9.9 billion of profits in North America offset by losses in other regions.
For 2023 IATA forecast $4.6 billion in profits for the industry globally.

Boeing and its suppliers experienced supply chain disruptions, labor instability and inflationary pressures that reduced productivity and adversely impacted financial position, results of operations and cash flows.
raw_excerpt: Airline financial performance, which influences demand for new capacity, has been adversely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA), net losses for the airline industry were $138 billion in 2020 and $42 billion in 2021.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — Boeing Capital segment: customer financing portfolio credit quality
key_points: BCC's gross customer financing and investment portfolio totaled $1,549 million at December 31, 2022.
A substantial portion of BCC's portfolio is composed of customers that have less than investment-grade credit.
BCC's portfolio is concentrated by varying degrees across Boeing aircraft product types, most notably 717 and 747-8 aircraft.
Approximately 4,950 western-built commercial jet aircraft (18.3% of current world fleet) were parked at the end of 2022.
At the end of 2021 and 2020, 20.5% and 29.4% of western-built commercial jet aircraft were parked, respectively.
Boeing states aircraft valuations could decline if significant numbers of additional aircraft are placed out of service.
BCC provided customer financing of $96 million during 2022 and none during 2021.
raw_excerpt: BCC's gross customer financing and investment portfolio at December 31, 2022 totaled $1,549 million. A substantial portion of BCC's portfolio is composed of customers that have less than investment-grade credit.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — BDS segment: long-term operating cycle makes period results non-indicative
key_points: Boeing states its operating cycle is long-term and involves many different types of development and production contracts with varying delivery and milestone schedules.
As a result, operating results of a particular period may not be indicative of future operating results.
Depending on the customer and their funding sources, orders may be structured as annual follow-on contracts, one large multi-year order, or a long-term award.
Period-to-period comparisons of backlog are not necessarily indicative of future workloads.
At the end of 2022, 28% of BDS backlog was attributable to non-U.S. customers.
raw_excerpt: Since our operating cycle is long-term and involves many different types of development and production contracts with varying delivery and milestone schedules, the operating results of a particular period may not be indicative of future operating results.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — BCA segment results: reach-forward losses and abnormal production costs
key_points: BCA revenues were $25,867M (2022), $19,493M (2021), $16,162M (2020), representing 39%, 31% and 28% of total company revenues respectively.
BCA loss from operations was $2,370M (2022), $6,475M (2021), $13,847M (2020); operating margins were (9.2)%, (33.2)%, (85.7)%.
The 2020 loss reflects a $6,493 million reach-forward loss on the 777X program, lower deliveries and lower program margins resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic.
The 2021 loss reflects a $3,460 million reach-forward loss on the 787 program and $1,887 million of abnormal production costs related to the 737 program.
Abnormal production costs in 2022 were $1,753 million, including $1,240 million for the 787 program, $325 million for the 777X program and $188 million for the 737 program.
BCA deliveries totaled 157 (2020), 340 (2021) and 480 (2022); 737 deliveries were 43 (2020), 263 (2021) and 387 (2022).
BCA research and development spending was $1,510M (2022), $1,140M (2021), $1,385M (2020).

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — 737 program production rate, inventory and delivery deferrals
key_points: Boeing increased the 737 production rate to 31 per month in 2022 and expects further gradual production rate increases based on market demand and supply chain capacity.
Boeing expensed abnormal production costs of $188 million and $1,887 million during 2022 and 2021 respectively on the 737 program.

Boeing continues to work with a small number of customers who have requested to defer deliveries or cancel orders for 737 MAX aircraft, and is remarketing and/or delaying deliveries of certain aircraft in inventory.
Boeing had approximately 250 aircraft in inventory as of December 31, 2022, including approximately 140 aircraft designated for customers in China.
Boeing anticipates delivering most of the aircraft in inventory by the end of 2024.
Undelivered units under firm orders at December 31, 2022 included 3,653 for the 737 program and 505 for the 787 program.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — BDS business environment: dependence on U.S. government discretionary appropriations
key_points: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 provided FY23 appropriations including $817 billion for the U.S. DoD and $25.4 billion for NASA.
FY23 appropriations included funding for Boeing programs including F/A-18 Super Hornet, F-15EX, CH-47 Chinook, AH-64 Apache, V-22 Osprey, KC-46A Tanker, MQ-25 and the Space Launch System.
The FY23 appropriations did not include funding for additional P-8 aircraft; the P-8 program continues to pursue sales to extend production beyond 2024.
Boeing states U.S. government discretionary spending, including defense spending, is likely to continue to be subject to pressure.

Future budget cuts or investment priority changes could result in reductions, cancellations and/or delays of existing contracts or programs, with material effect on results of operations, financial position and/or cash flows.
There is ongoing uncertainty with respect to program-level appropriations for FY2024 and beyond.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — Item 1 Business: company description and Boeing Capital segment role
key_points: Boeing describes itself as one of the world's major producers of commercial aircraft, offering a family of commercial jetliners for airlines' global passenger and cargo requirements.
Aircraft in production include the 737 narrow-body and the 767, 777 and 787 wide-body models; production of the 747 wide-body ended in 2022.

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — Item 7 MD&A, Overview（行业需求驱动因素与外部冲击）
key_points: Boeing 将 air travel demand 的基本驱动因素列为：economic growth、因贸易与全球化提升的出行倾向、以及航空权自由化带来的航线服务改善。
Boeing 的 Commercial Market Outlook 预测 20 年客运与货运流量年增长 3.8%，该预测基于全球 GDP 年均增长 2.6% 的长期假设。
基于上述假设，Boeing 预测未来 20 年约 41,170 架新飞机需求。
Boeing 明确表述行业「remains vulnerable to exogenous developments」，并列举 fuel price spikes、credit market shocks、恐怖主义、自然灾害、冲突、流行病/大流行、环境监管收紧。
raw_excerpt: The long-term outlook for the industry remains positive due to the fundamental drivers of air travel demand: economic growth, increasing propensity to travel due to increased trade, globalization and improved airline services driven by liberalization of air traffic rights between countries. Our Commercial Market Outlook forecast projects a 3.8% growth rate for passenger and cargo traffic over a 20-year period. Based on long-term global economic growth projections of 2.6% in average annual gross domestic product, we project demand for approximately 41,170 new airplanes over the next 20 years. The industry remains vulnerable to exogenous developments including fuel price spikes, credit market shocks, acts of terrorism, natural disasters, conflicts, epidemics, pandemics and increased global environmental regulations.

Boeing 转引 IATA 数据：全球航空业净亏损 2020 年为 1,380 亿美元、2021 年为 420 亿美元。
Boeing 转引 IATA 预测：2022 年全球航空业亏损 69 亿美元，其中北美盈利约 99 亿美元。
注意：上述 IATA 数字为 Boeing 10-K 的转引，非 IATA 一手报告。

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — Backlog 附注（订单可取消性与积压订单脆弱性）
key_points: Boeing 的 contractual backlog 明确排除购买选择权、未签署正式合同的已宣布订单、以及客户拥有单方面终止权的订单。
Boeing 警告：若长期无法在中国交付 737 MAX，或 777X / 737-7 / 737-10 投入服务进一步延迟，「we may experience reductions to backlog and/or significant order cancellations」。
Commercial Airplanes backlog：2022 年末 3,298.24 亿美元，2021 年末 2,968.82 亿美元。
公司总 backlog：2022 年末 4,043.81 亿美元，2021 年末 3,774.99 亿美元；其中 contractual backlog 3,819.77 / 3,563.62 亿美元。

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — 737/787 项目生产速率与供应链约束（p33、p9）
key_points: 737 生产率 2022 年提升至 31 架/月，后续提升将「based on market demand and supply chain capacity」。
737 项目在维持 31 架/月时遭遇运营与供应链挑战；公司计划依据市场需求与供应链产能逐步提产。
787 因供应链质量问题于 2021 年 5 月暂停交付；2021Q3 公司判定低于 5 架/月的生产率为 abnormally low production rates，产生异常生产成本。
787 累计异常成本至 2022 年末为 17 亿美元，2022Q4 将总额估计上调至 28 亿美元，主因供应链约束导致近期减产及检验返工成本上升。
公司称将继续与客户和供应商就未来交付时点与生产速率变化进行协调。

title: The Boeing Company 2022 Form 10-K — 客户融资承诺与停场机队（信贷条件与资产价值线索，p89、p41）
key_points: 飞机订单相关融资承诺（含选择权与销售活动中提议的订单、已交付飞机再融资）合计 161.05 亿美元，2021 年为 129.05 亿美元。
截至 2022 年末，全部融资承诺均关联于 Boeing 认为信用评级低于投资级的客户。
Boeing Capital 的客户融资与投资组合 2022 年末为 15.49 亿美元，相当部分客户低于投资级，且组合集中于 717、747-8 等机型。
2022 年末约 4,950 架西方制造商用喷气机停场，占全球机队 18.3%；2021 年末与 2020 年末分别为 20.5% 与 29.4%。
Boeing 称飞机价值与租赁费率受停场飞机数量与机型影响，停场规模直接影响新机交付数量、客户履约能力与组合内飞机价值。

title: BOEING_2022_10K — BCA backlog 讨论（订单取消与 ASC 606 调整）
key_points: 2022 年飞机订单取消合计 $11,251M，涉及 737 与 787 机型。

title: BOEING_2022_10K — Program Highlights（各机型生产速率与库存）
key_points: 737 生产速率于 2022 年提升至 31 架/月，公司计划基于市场需求与供应链能力进一步逐步提升。
767 项目（含 KC-46A 衍生型）合计生产速率 3 架/月；777/777X 合计生产速率 3 架/月。
787 处于低速率生产，公司预计 2023 年逐步回到 5 架/月；低于 5 架/月被视为异常低速率并产生异常生产成本。
777X-9 生产于 2022 年第二季度起暂停（2022–2023 年），预计产生约 $1.5B 异常生产成本。
2022 年末 737 项目库存约 250 架，其中约 140 架指定给中国客户；787 库存约 100 架（2021 年末约 110 架）。

title: BOEING_2022_10K — Accounting quantities and firm orders by program（未交付确定订单）
BOEING_2022_10K — MD&A Overview（行业长期需求、外生冲击风险、转引 IATA 数据）
key_points: 公司称行业长期前景依然正面，Commercial Market Outlook 预测 20 年客运与货运量年增 3.8%，20 年需求约 41,170 架新飞机（基于 2.6% 年均全球 GDP 增长假设）。
公司称行业仍易受外生冲击影响，列举油价飙升、信贷市场冲击、恐怖主义、自然灾害、冲突、流行病/大流行病及环境监管加强。
转引 IATA：2020 年行业净亏损 $138B、2021 年 $42B；IATA 预测 2022 年全球亏损 $6.9B（北美盈利约 $9.9B），2023 年全球盈利 $4.6B。
2022 年 BGS 商业服务量已恢复至疫情前水平，公司预计后续季度 BGS 商业收入保持强劲；政府服务需求展望稳定。
公司称与供应商正经历供应链中断、劳动力不稳定与通胀压力，这些因素降低了整体生产率并负面影响财务表现。

title: BOEING_2022_10K — 认证与交付节奏（FAA 授权、机型取证时间表）
key_points: 787 于 2022 年 7 月 28 日获 FAA 授权恢复交付，8 月恢复交付，2022 年交付 31 架。
公司当时预计 737-7 于 2023 年取证并交付，737-10 于 2023 年开始 FAA 认证试飞、2024 年首交付。
777X-9 首交付推迟至 2025 年，777X-8F 首交付预计 2027 年。
公司称认证时间最终由监管机构决定，取证延迟可能对收入、现金流与经营结果产生不利影响。

During 2022, we delivered 31 aircraft to customers. … 236 737-7 and 720 737-10 aircraft in backlog … 777X-9 2013 2025 / 777X-8F 2022 2027 … The timing of certifications will ultimately be determined by the regulators.

title: BOEING_2022_10K — BCA Business Environment and Trends（竞争、市场份额、Airbus 与 COMAC）
key_points: BCA 订单簿按金额约 70% 来自非美国航空公司。
公司称 2019 年 737 MAX 停飞及多辖区交付暂停显著降低了其在单通道飞机交付方面的市场份额，并可能为竞争对手提供获取更多订单的机会。
Airbus 在 2018 年收购 Bombardier C 系列（现 A220）多数股权后，继续扩展 100–150 座跨大陆市场。
COMAC 于 2022 年交付首架 C919 飞机。
公司称该市场环境造成价格等方面的激烈压力，并预计这些压力将持续或加剧。
raw_excerpt: Approximately 70% of Commercial Airplanes' total backlog, in dollar terms, is with non-U.S. airlines. … the grounding of the 737 MAX in 2019 and the associated suspension of 737 MAX deliveries in multiple jurisdictions significantly reduced our market share with respect to deliveries of single aisle aircraft and may provide competitors with an opportunity to obtain more orders and increase market share. … COMAC, which delivered its first C919 aircraft in 2022.
